info.title: wan-nee-la
info.summary: Employee leave tracker — the endpoints that answer in JSON.
info.description:
Two things are worth knowing before calling anything here.

**Every route except `/line/webhook` sits behind Cloudflare Access**, which
authenticates at the edge, before the Worker runs. There is no API key and
no signup: an Access identity the app has not seen becomes a user on its
first request, with the current year's quotas seeded. Access *service
tokens* deliberately cannot use the app — a token has no email, and every
row here is keyed by one.

**Mutations require an `Origin` header matching `Host`.** Access is an
authentication gate, not a CSRF defence: its cookie rides along on a form
post from any origin. A missing `Origin` is refused rather than waved
through, so a non-browser client must send one explicitly. `/line/webhook`
is the exception and proves itself with an HMAC signature instead.

servers.description: The deployment. One per company; there is no shared instance.

get.summary: Which build answered, and whether D1 responds
get.description:
Registered above the authentication middleware, so it needs no user —
but it is still behind Access at the edge, which is why an anonymous
uptime check cannot reach it without a Bypass rule on this path.

Deliberately dull: it leaks nothing about who works here or when they
are away. `devAuthBypass` is surfaced precisely so a production check
can catch the local development bypass being left switched on.

200.description:
The Worker is up and D1 answered. When D1 does not, the same body
comes back with a 503 instead — see below — so "the Worker is down"
and "the Worker is up and D1 is not" stay distinguishable either by
status or by `ok` and `db`.

version.description: Worker version id, from Cloudflare's version metadata binding.

bangkokToday.description:
Today in Asia/Bangkok, which is the only "today" this app
recognises. Workers run in UTC, and between 17:00 and
23:59 UTC that is yesterday in Bangkok.

accessConfigured.description: Both ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN and ACCESS_AUD are set.

devAuthBypass.description:
True means identity verification is switched off and every
visitor is signed in as DEV_EMAIL. Must never be true in
production; this field exists so a check can assert that.

503.description:
D1 did not answer. The body is the same shape, with `ok` and `db`
false — a separate status so a monitor that reads only the status
code still notices.

get.summary: Everyone's confirmed leave over a date range
get.description:
The shared calendar as data. Cancelled bookings are absent, and so are
deactivated people — those surfaces answer "who of us is out", and a
former employee is not one of us.

Emails are not in the feed. A name and a leave type are what the
calendar shows; an address is what turns a leave tracker into a
directory.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Inclusive. Anything that is not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD` falls back to
the first of the current Bangkok month rather than erroring.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive. Defaults to the last day of the current Bangkok month.

200.description: The range, echoed back, and the entries inside it.

get.summary: What a booking would cost, and who else is already away
get.description:
The booking form's live preview. The client asks rather than counting
locally: a second copy of the half-day and holiday rules would drift,
and the number shown before submitting would stop matching the number
the quota is actually charged.

Coverage is advisory. Nothing here can refuse a booking — the app does
not know who covers for whom. It reports the *worst single day* in the
range rather than a total, because five people out on five separate
days is a normal week and five people out on the same Tuesday is the
thing worth seeing before you book.

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description:
A booking id to leave out of the coverage count. Set when editing,
so the booking being changed is not reported as somebody else
already away on those days.

200.description:
**Always 200, including when the input is rejected.** A preview that
cannot be computed is not a transport failure, and this endpoint
fires on every keystroke in a date field — half of what it is asked
is a half-typed date. Check for the `error` member, not the status.

counted.summary: A costed range with a coverage warning

error.message: That range has no working days in it.

post.summary: Register this browser for the morning digest
post.description:
Stored against the caller's own identity. One person may have several
browsers subscribed; each is a separate row keyed by its endpoint.

400.description: The body is not a usable push subscription.

post.description:
Scoped to the owner. A push endpoint is not a secret — it travels to
the push service on every send — so knowing someone else's must not let
you silence their notifications.

200.description:
Returned whether or not a row was actually deleted. By this point
the browser has already unsubscribed locally, so reporting a
failure would only invite it to retry something that can never
succeed.

post.summary: Send a test notification to the caller's own browsers
post.description:
Without this, the only way to learn whether push works is to wait until
08:00 the next working day — which is how a broken setup stays broken.

Sends to every browser the caller has subscribed, and prunes any the
push service reports as gone. A test is exactly when a stale
subscription surfaces.

200.description: At least one browser accepted it.

delivered.description: How many browsers accepted the push.

409.description: This account has no subscriptions yet.

503.description: The server has no VAPID pair configured.

post.summary: Capture the group id LINE will not show you
post.description:
The one publicly reachable route in the app: LINE's servers must reach
it and cannot carry an Access token, so it needs a Bypass rule on this
path in the Access policy.

It therefore defends itself. The raw body is read exactly once and its
HMAC checked before anything is parsed — `json()` consumes the stream,
and a later re-read would verify the signature over an empty body. An
unsigned request is refused outright rather than logged and allowed.

The only state it may write is the group id, which is not visible in
the LINE app and arrives here as `source.groupId` on a `join` or
`message` event. Capture it once and this route has done its job.

requestBody.description: A LINE Messaging API webhook payload.

200.description:
Acknowledged — including when the event carried nothing wanted.
LINE retries on any non-2xx, and a retry is how a group gets two
copies of the 08:00 post.

400.description: Body is not JSON. Signature had already passed.

503.description: No LINE channel secret configured on this deployment.

cloudflareAccess.name: CF_Authorization
cloudflareAccess.description:
Issued by Cloudflare Access on sign-in and verified against the
application's audience before the Worker runs. The Worker also accepts
the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` header, which is what Access forwards.

Not something a client mints. There is no token endpoint here, and
Access service tokens are refused by design: a service token carries no
email, and every row in this app is keyed by one.

lineSignature.name: X-Line-Signature
lineSignature.description:
base64(HMAC-SHA256(raw request body, LINE channel secret)), compared in
constant time. Applies to `/line/webhook` alone.

CrossOrigin.description:
`Origin` was absent, or did not match `Host`. Every browser sends
`Origin` on a POST, so absence means something that is not one of our
pages — and "allow when the header is missing" is the standard way this
check is quietly defeated.

Date.description: A calendar date in Asia/Bangkok. No time, no zone — leave is booked in days.

Half.description:
Which half of the boundary day is taken. A multi-day booking cannot
start `am` or end `pm` — that would be a range with a hole at one end.

name.description: Display name. The email is deliberately not in this feed.

label.description: English label of the leave type.

color.description: The type's calendar colour, mixed into the chip background.

days.description:
Working days charged, holidays and weekends removed. Halves make it
fractional, so 0.5 and 3.5 are ordinary values.

note.description:
Null when the booking has no note *and* when it has a private one.
A private note is absent from the feed rather than hidden by
whatever renders it — the alternative tells a colleague that a note
they may not read exists.

days.description: Working days the range would cost.

date.description:
The worst day, already formatted in the caller's language —
a client would otherwise need month names in two languages
to turn 2026-08-24 into 24 ส.ค.

out.description: People away that day, including the caller.

busy.description:
True once `out` reaches a third of the roster, and never at
fewer than two people — so the warning neither fires on one
colleague in a team of forty nor stays silent when both
halves of a team of two book the same Tuesday.

error.description:
A message *key*, not a sentence. Booking rules are pure functions
with no idea which language the request arrived in, so they name
the message and the caller renders it. Note this differs from the
`error` of `/api/leave`, which is a plain string.

message.description:
The same message rendered in the caller's language, ready to
show. The booking form displays this; a program can use `key`.
examples: That day is a weekend or a public holiday.

vars.description: Values to substitute into the message's placeholders.

p256dh.description: The client's public key, base64url, uncompressed P-256 point.
